objects.description: Concrete math expression parser class in namespace mu. Inherits from ParserBase (declared in included headers). Provides initialization hooks for character sets, functions, constants, and operators, a variable-detection callback, numerical differentiation (Diff), and a helper to parse numeric values (IsVal). The actual types string_type, value_type, and char_type, as well as ownership/lifetime rules, are defined in included headers. Construction is via the default constructor; destruction/virtual dtor presumed in base. Details like thread safety and copy/move semantics are not specified here.

Core C++ class implementing the muparser base engine. Parses mathematical expressions into bytecode and evaluates them. Provides APIs to define variables, constants, functions, and operators, configure locale and character sets, and evaluate expressions (single or bulk). Abstract hooks (InitCharSets/InitFun/InitConst/InitOprt) allow derived classes to register built-ins. Ownership: internally manages a ParserTokenReader via unique_ptr and stores bytecode and definitions. Construction via public constructors; destruction via virtual destructor.

Final concrete token reader used by mu::ParserBase to tokenize mathematical expressions. It owns parsing state, syntax flags, used-variable tracking, and provides ReadNextToken along with helpers for identifying token kinds and handling variable creation via a factory. Construction requires a ParserBase* parent. Copy operations are declared private; cloning is provided via Clone(ParserBase*). Details of value_type, string_type, and maps are defined in included headers.

Token used by the parser bytecode to represent one RPN instruction. It stores the command code (Cmd) and a union with payload for values (pointers and literals), functions (erased callable, argument count, and optional index for string functions), or operators (pointer and offset). Details of ECmdCode, value_type, and generic_callable_type are defined elsewhere.

Final bytecode container for the mu parser. Holds the reverse polish notation program (vector of SToken), associated expression and string buffer, and provides methods to build, optimize, finalize, and query the bytecode. Construction is via default or copy; building occurs through AddVar/AddVal/AddOp/AddFun variants; Finalize prepares the program. Throws ParserError if accessed when empty.

functions.name: mu::Parser::Parser
functions.signature: mu::Parser::Parser()
functions.description: Default constructor for the mu::Parser class, the standard floating-point expression parser. Typically prepares the parser for use by initializing built-in character sets, operators, functions, and constants (via base-class initialization routines).
requirements: No arguments; constructs a new parser instance in default state.
Subsequent use generally requires setting an expression and optional variables/constants before evaluation (details depend on ParserBase).

functions.name: mu::Parser::InitCharSets
functions.signature: void mu::Parser::InitCharSets()
functions.description: Initializes the parser’s character-class sets (e.g., valid identifier characters, whitespace, etc.). This method overrides the base implementation to set up the default character policies for mu::Parser.
requirements: Should be called before tokenization/parsing if character sets were modified or not yet initialized.
Calling on a fully constructed mu::Parser instance is required.
Intended primarily for internal use during parser setup; external calls may reinitialize internal state.

functions.name: mu::Parser::InitFun
functions.signature: void mu::Parser::InitFun()
functions.description: Registers the set of built-in functions supported by the standard mu::Parser (e.g., math functions). Overrides the base to populate the function table used during parsing and evaluation.
requirements: Call only on a valid, constructed parser instance.
Should be called before parsing/evaluation if built-in functions are not yet registered or after a reset/clear.
Intended primarily for internal initialization; external reinitialization may overwrite/replace previous function registrations.

functions.name: mu::Parser::InitConst
functions.signature: void mu::Parser::InitConst()
functions.description: Registers the set of built-in constants for mu::Parser (e.g., mathematical constants). Overrides the base to populate the constant table used during parsing and evaluation.
requirements: Call only on a valid, constructed parser instance.
Should be called before parsing/evaluation if constants are not yet registered or after a reset/clear.
External reinitialization may overwrite/replace existing constant registrations.

functions.name: mu::Parser::InitOprt
functions.signature: void mu::Parser::InitOprt()
functions.description: Registers the built-in operators (prefix, infix, postfix as applicable) supported by mu::Parser. Overrides the base to populate the operator set used by the tokenizer and evaluator.
requirements: Call only on a valid, constructed parser instance.
Should be called before parsing/evaluation if operators are not yet registered or after a reset/clear.
External reinitialization may change operator definitions and affect parsing behavior.

functions.name: mu::Parser::OnDetectVar
functions.signature: void mu::Parser::OnDetectVar(string_type* pExpr, int& nStart, int& nEnd)
functions.description: Callback hook invoked when the tokenizer detects a variable token in the expression. Allows the parser to validate or adjust variable detection within the expression substring [nStart, nEnd).
requirements: pExpr must be a non-null pointer to the expression string being parsed.
nStart and nEnd must refer to valid indices within *pExpr (0 <= nStart <= nEnd <= pExpr->length()).
Intended for internal use by the parser during tokenization; caller-supplied usage should ensure indices remain consistent if modified.

functions.name: mu::Parser::Diff
functions.signature: value_type mu::Parser::Diff(value_type* a_Var, value_type a_fPos, value_type a_fEpsilon = 0) const
functions.description: Computes the numerical derivative of the current expression with respect to the variable referenced by a_Var at position a_fPos. If a_fEpsilon is 0, an internal default step is used; otherwise, the provided step size is used for the finite-difference calculation.
requirements: a_Var must be a valid, non-null pointer to a parser variable (i.e., a variable previously bound/registered with this parser).
The parser must have a valid expression set that depends on the referenced variable for meaningful results.
a_fEpsilon should be non-negative; if 0, the function chooses a default step size.
Evaluation of the expression at perturbed points around a_fPos must be valid (e.g., no domain errors for those inputs).

functions.name: mupCreate

functions.description: Invokes the stored numerical function with exactly NbParams arguments, forwarding the provided arguments. If user data was bound when the callable was created, the user-data variant of the function is called; otherwise the plain function pointer is used. functions.name: mu::generic_callable_type::call_bulkfun

Uses the user-data variant if user data is present. Provided to call bulkfun_typeN/bulkfun_userdata_typeN registered with muParser.
requirements: Template parameter NbParams must equal sizeof...(Args) - 2; enforced via static_assert.
_pRawFun must point to a bulk function of the expected signature (bulkfun_typeN or bulkfun_userdata_typeN for the chosen NbParams).
If _pUserData is non-null, the function must be the user-data bulk variant; otherwise the plain bulk function variant is required.
Behavior is undefined if _pRawFun is null; callers should check operator bool() before calling.
The two extra arguments beyond NbParams must match the registered bulk function’s expected leading parameters (exact types as registered).

requirements: _pRawFun must point to a valid mult-arity function compatible with multfun_type or multfun_userdata_type.
a_afArg must point to an array of at least a_iArgc elements of value_type; must not be null when a_iArgc > 0.
a_iArgc must be the actual number of arguments provided via a_afArg; negative values are invalid.
If _pUserData is non-null, the function must be the user-data variant; otherwise it must be the plain variant.
Callers should ensure operator bool() returns true before calling to avoid null function pointer usage.

import random
import math
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for valid muParser mathematical expression strings.
# Focus: produce expressions that are likely valid across both C and C++ APIs
# and exercise variable detection, SetExpr/SetFormula, and C-API mupSetExpr.
# Strategy:
# - ASCII-only output to map cleanly to muChar_t (char or wchar_t)
# - Build from a small set of safe numeric literals, variables, operators,
#   standard functions, and parentheses.
# - Ensure presence of at least one identifier-like token (e.g., variable "x")
#   to trigger OnDetectVar hook paths.
# - Vary locales lightly by occasionally inserting argument separators ','
#   and using decimal points.
# - Keep size <= 512 (well under 4096 limit and fuzzer downsizing).

SAFE_VARS = [
    "x", "y", "z", "a1", "b2", "alpha", "beta", "gamma",
]

SAFE_CONSTS = [
    "pi", "e"
]

SAFE_FUNCS_UNARY = [
    "sin", "cos", "tan", "sqrt", "abs", "log", "log10", "exp"
]

SAFE_FUNCS_BINARY = [
    "min", "max", "atan2", "pow"
]

SAFE_MULTI_FUNCS = [
    "sum", "avg"
]

SAFE_POSTFIX = [
    # muParser has postfix operators in tests like Mega, Micro, Milli when defined.
    # Keep postfix use optional and sparse; not all builds register them.
]

SAFE_BIN_OPS = [
    "+", "-", "*", "/", "^", "<", "<=", ">", ">=", "==", "!=", "&&", "||"
]

SAFE_INFIX = [
    # Typically unary + and unary - are supported; we use them via expression layout.
]

DIGITS = "0123456789"


def rand_float_literal(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a numeric literal within a safe range with optional decimal part.
    sign = rng.choice(["", "-", "+"]) if rng.random() < 0.2 else ""
    # Keep magnitudes moderate to avoid domain issues in functions
    whole = str(rng.randint(0, 1000))
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        frac_len = rng.randint(1, 4)
        frac = ''.join(rng.choice(DIGITS) for _ in range(frac_len))
        return f"{sign}{whole}.{frac}"
    else:
        return f"{sign}{whole}"


def rand_var(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(SAFE_VARS)


def rand_atom(rng: random.Random, ensure_identifier: bool) -> Tuple[str, bool]:
    # Returns (text, has_identifier)
    choice = rng.random()
    if ensure_identifier or choice < 0.35:
        v = rand_var(rng)
        return v, True
    elif choice < 0.65:
        return rand_float_literal(rng), False
    else:
        # Optional constant by name
        c = rng.choice(SAFE_CONSTS)
        return c, True


def call_unary(func: str, arg: str) -> str:
    return f"{func}({arg})"


def call_binary(func: str, arg1: str, arg2: str) -> str:
    return f"{func}({arg1},{arg2})"


def call_multi(func: str, args: List[str]) -> str:
    return f"{func}(" + ",".join(args) + ")"


def maybe_parenthesize(rng: random.Random, expr: str) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        return f"({expr})"
    return expr


def build_term(rng: random.Random, depth: int, need_ident: bool) -> Tuple[str, bool]:
    # Recursively build a term. Keep depth small to fit bounds.
    if depth <= 0:
        return rand_atom(rng, need_ident)

    r = rng.random()
    # Try function calls often to exercise SetFormula/SetExpr parsing.
    if r < 0.35:
        # Unary function
        func = rng.choice(SAFE_FUNCS_UNARY)
        arg, has_id = build_term(rng, depth - 1, need_ident)
        return call_unary(func, arg), has_id or True  # function identifier present
    elif r < 0.55:
        # Binary function
        func = rng.choice(SAFE_FUNCS_BINARY)
        arg1, id1 = build_term(rng, depth - 1, need_ident)
        arg2, id2 = build_term(rng, depth - 1, need_ident and not id1)
        return call_binary(func, arg1, arg2), id1 or id2 or True
    elif r < 0.7:
        # Multi-arg function
        func = rng.choice(SAFE_MULTI_FUNCS)
        n = rng.randint(2, 5)
        parts: List[str] = []
        has_id = False
        for i in range(n):
            part, pid = build_term(rng, depth - 1, need_ident and not has_id)
            parts.append(part)
            has_id = has_id or pid
        return call_multi(func, parts), has_id or True
    else:
        # Compose binary operator expression
        left, idl = build_term(rng, depth - 1, need_ident)
        right, idr = build_term(rng, depth - 1, need_ident and not idl)
        op = rng.choice(SAFE_BIN_OPS)
        expr = f"{maybe_parenthesize(rng, left)} {op} {maybe_parenthesize(rng, right)}"
        return expr, idl or idr


def ensure_contains_x(expr: str) -> str:
    # Append a simple pattern containing 'x' to ensure an identifier-like token exists for OnDetectVar
    if 'x' not in expr:
        # Append with whitespace to become a separate token
        expr = expr + " + x"
    return expr


def tidy(expr: str, max_len: int = 400) -> str:
    # Reduce sequences of spaces and limit size
    expr = ' '.join(expr.split())
    if len(expr) > max_len:
        expr = expr[:max_len]
    return expr


def assemble_expression(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build 1..3 top-level clauses joined by operators or commas to vary syntax.
    k = rng.randint(1, 3)
    parts: List[str] = []
    has_id = False
    for i in range(k):
        term, tid = build_term(rng, depth=rng.randint(1, 3), need_ident=not has_id)
        parts.append(term)
        has_id = has_id or tid
    if k == 1:
        expr = parts[0]
    else:
        joiner = rng.choice([" + ", " - ", ","])  # include ',' to exercise argument separator paths
        expr = joiner.join(parts)
    # Occasionally wrap whole expression
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        expr = f"({expr})"
    expr = ensure_contains_x(expr)
    expr = tidy(expr)
    return expr


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    expr = assemble_expression(rng)
    # Ensure non-empty and ASCII-only; mu C-API requires zero-terminated muChar_t*
    if not expr:
        expr = "0"
    # Append newline or semicolon rarely to vary but still generally valid (muParser ignores whitespace)
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        expr += "\n"
    # Return as bytes (ASCII). Non-ASCII avoided deliberately.
    data = expr.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')
    # Bound to <= 512 as fuzzers will further bound; also < 4096 requirement
    if len(data) > 512:
        data = data[:512]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: identifier/name string (muChar_t*, zero-terminated),
# used to name functions/operators/variables/constants. Fuzzer truncates
# to small sizes (mostly 4..16) and replaces embedded NUL with a fallback
# character. We'll provide ASCII-friendly names with variations to trigger
# different code paths, including: short/long, letters, digits, underscores,
# operator-like symbols for operator charsets, and single-char choices for
# sep/dec/thousands setters.

# Buffer format we emit:
# A sequence of entries to be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int).
# We cannot control the exact call order, so we craft a pool of varied strings
# concatenated with separators. The fuzzer harness typically reads raw bytes
# and splits greedily; a safe approach is to provide multiple NUL-terminated
# chunks. We avoid embedded NUL inside chunks (the harness replaces them).
# Limit total size <= 4096 bytes.

SEPARATORS = [',', ';', '|', ':']

def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 16) -> str:
    # Valid identifier: letters, digits, underscore, starting with letter/_
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + '_')
    rest_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '_'
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = first + ''.join(rng.choice(rest_chars) for _ in range(max(0, length - 1)))
    return s

def _rand_op_symbol(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 4) -> str:
    # Operator characters commonly acceptable by muparser operator charset
    ops = "+-*/%^<>=!&|~?:"
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(ops) for _ in range(length))

def _rand_charset(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 24) -> str:
    # Build a plausible charset string: include letters, digits, underscore, and some ops
    chars = []
    # Ensure a mix
    chars.extend(rng.sample(string.ascii_lowercase, k=min(5, len(string.ascii_lowercase))))
    chars.extend(rng.sample(string.ascii_uppercase, k=5))
    chars.extend(rng.sample(string.digits, k=5))
    chars.extend(rng.sample(list("_+-*/!~^"), k=5))
    rng.shuffle(chars)
    return ''.join(chars)[:max_len]

def _basic_pool(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    pool: List[str] = []
    # A set of valid identifiers
    for _ in range(12):
        pool.append(_rand_ident(rng))
    # Very short identifiers to satisfy empty->fallback paths
    pool.extend(['f', 'g', 'h', 'i', 'j', 'k', 'l', 'm', 'n', 'o', 'p', 'x', 'K', 'S'])
    # Operator-like symbols for DefineOprt/Define(Infix|Postfix)Oprt and charset setters
    for _ in range(6):
        pool.append(_rand_op_symbol(rng))
    pool.extend(['+', '!', '~'])
    # Charsets (up to 32 filtered in stubs)
    for _ in range(4):
        pool.append(_rand_charset(rng, max_len=rng.randint(12, 28)))
    # Strings for string-constants and string-functions (non-empty, printable, <=64/256 trimmed by stubs)
    alpha = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-./"
    for ln in (5, 11, 23, 47, 63, 127, 191):
        s = ''.join(rng.choice(alpha) for _ in range(ln))
        pool.append(s)
    # Single-character entries for separators/decimal/thousands
    pool.extend([",", ".", " ", ";", ":"])
    # Ensure diversity and no embedded NULs
    return pool

def _encode_mu_char_chunks(chunks: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join as NUL-terminated chunks, with occasional extra separators to aid splitting
    out = bytearray()
    for i, s in enumerate(chunks):
        # Avoid internal NUL; sanitize to ASCII, replace any accidental NUL
        bs = s.encode('ascii', errors='ignore').replace(b"\x00", b"_")
        out += bs
        out.append(0)  # NUL terminate each chunk for robust consumption
        if i % 7 == 6:
            # Insert an additional delimiter block occasionally
            out += b"--" + bytes([0])
    return bytes(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    pool = _basic_pool(rng)
    # Add some duplicates with slight variations to explore truncation effects
    variants: List[str] = []
    for s in rng.sample(pool, k=min(10, len(pool))):
        # extend or shorten
        if len(s) < 16:
            pad = _rand_ident(rng, 1, 6)
            variants.append((s + pad)[:16])
        else:
            variants.append(s[:16])
    pool.extend(variants)
    # Shuffle to vary consumption order
    rng.shuffle(pool)
    data = _encode_mu_char_chunks(pool)
    # Cap at 4096 bytes
    return data[:4096]

import random
import struct
import itertools

# We generate arbitrary byte strings that will be cast byte-by-byte to mu::char_type
# and used as mu::string_type in several contexts:
# - ParserToken::SetString(s, size): any bytes acceptable, but interesting if size differs
# - generic_callable_type::call_strfun: the string is parsed via stringstream to a number
#   so providing strings that can parse to numbers (including signs, decimals, exponents),
#   also with leading/trailing spaces, thousand separators, locales, NaNs/Inf, and very long digits,
#   can exercise different code paths.
# - ParserToken::GetAsString: equality with original text; any bytes fine.
#
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR takes the entire buffer. We'll encode multiple cases in one buffer by
# concatenating segments with separators so the harness can slice different calls; however,
# many fuzzers feed the same buffer to multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR invocations sequentially, often
# consuming bytes incrementally. To keep inputs valid regardless, we prepare a single
# robust string that works for all uses.
#
# Strategy:
# - Build a composite ASCII-like numeric string with optional sign, integer/frac, exponent.
# - Randomly include whitespace, plus/minus, scientific notation, leading zeros, very long runs.
# - Optionally include special tokens: "nan", "inf", localized decimal "," and arg-sep variations.
# - Ensure size <= 4096.
#
# The buffer is raw bytes; no trailing NUL is necessary (std::string used in stub).

DIGITS = b"0123456789"
WS = b" \t\r\n\v\f"
SIGNS = [b"", b"+", b"-"]


def _rand_choice(rng, seq):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def _make_numeric_string(rng):
    parts = []
    # Optional leading whitespace
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(rng.choice([b"", b" ", b"\t", b"\n"]) * rng.randint(0, 4))
    # Optional sign
    parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, SIGNS))
    # Integer part
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        parts.append(b"0")
    else:
        n_digits = rng.randint(1, 24)
        parts.append(bytes(rng.choice(DIGITS) for _ in range(n_digits)))
    # Fractional part
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        # Choose between dot and comma to exercise locale handling
        sep = b"," if rng.random() < 0.2 else b"."
        parts.append(sep)
        n_frac = rng.randint(0, 24)
        parts.append(bytes(rng.choice(DIGITS) for _ in range(n_frac)))
    # Exponent
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, [b"e", b"E"]))
        parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, SIGNS))
        parts.append(bytes(rng.choice(DIGITS) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))))
    # Trailing whitespace
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(rng.choice([b"", b" ", b"\t", b"\n"]) * rng.randint(0, 4))
    return b"".join(parts)


def _make_special_numeric(rng):
    specials = [b"nan", b"NaN", b"NAN", b"inf", b"Inf", b"INF",
                b"+inf", b"-inf", b"+INF", b"-INF"]
    return _rand_choice(rng, specials)


def _insert_noise(rng, s: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Insert some operator-like and random bytes that should be preserved but still parse prefix number
    noise_pool = [b"", b" ", b"_", b"x", b";", b",", b"@", b"#"]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s = _rand_choice(rng, noise_pool) + s
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s = s + _rand_choice(rng, noise_pool)
    return s


def _make_long_digit_run(rng):
    n = rng.randint(32, 256)
    return bytes(rng.choice(DIGITS) for _ in range(n))


def _make_payload(rng):
    # Compose multiple candidates separated by newlines so any split still yields a number
    segments = []
    # 1) Standard numeric
    segments.append(_insert_noise(rng, _make_numeric_string(rng)))
    # 2) Special (nan/inf)
    segments.append(_insert_noise(rng, _make_special_numeric(rng)))
    # 3) Long integer
    segments.append(_insert_noise(rng, _make_long_digit_run(rng)))
    # 4) Scientific with many frac digits
    segments.append(_insert_noise(rng, _make_numeric_string(rng)))
    # 5) Locale-style with comma decimal
    s = _make_numeric_string(rng)
    if b"," not in s:
        s = s.replace(b".", b",", 1) if b"." in s else b"1,234"
    segments.append(_insert_noise(rng, s))
    # Join with newlines and commas to exercise separators; these bytes are kept as-is
    buf = b"\n".join(segments)
    # Ensure size cap
    return buf[:4000]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Randomly decide to return either composite payload or a single focused case
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.4:
        return _make_payload(rng)
    elif choice < 0.7:
        return _insert_noise(rng, _make_numeric_string(rng))[:4000]
    else:
        return _insert_noise(rng, _make_special_numeric(rng))[:4000]
